scope: CPU trajectory packing microbenchmark, not end-to-end training

fixture.description: Collect the first 128 completed episodes from NativePool.round using a shared context DMCModel with hidden width 16. Epsilon 1 bypasses value inference. Reuse these exact episode records, payoffs and auxiliary labels for both writers.

implementations.baseline: Original flush: for each role and complete T-step unroll, take one free slot, create np.asarray for every field, torch.as_tensor(block), then shared_tensor[index].copy_ and publish the index.
implementations.optimized: Cache NumPy views of CPU shared tensors. Take up to min(16, max(1, 320 // T)) available slots per group. Build each field with its final storage dtype, scatter the grouped unrolls into the NumPy view, then publish each completed slot separately.

method.queues: queue.Queue in one process; multiprocessing serialization and process scheduling excluded
method.allocation: Shared buffers, queues and writer construction excluded from timer
method.correctness: For the fully accumulated episode fixture, compare every published state, action, target, done, episode_return and aux_target tensor to the baseline with rtol=0 and atol=0; all matched.
method.pending_tail: Incomplete unrolls remain pending in both writers. Input sample count includes these tails; published sample count was not recorded.

limitations: These ratios measure only trajectory packing, not total training throughput.
This Windows laptop CPU differs from the PVE training server CPU.
Results use one fixed rollout seed and exploration-only complete episodes.
Queue IPC, actor inference, GPU transfers, learner updates and weight publication are excluded.
Only the six-run medians were retained; individual repetition durations are unavailable.
